headline: Foundation models add mechanistic and oracle constraints to RNA, antibody and TCR tasks
label: Constrained Biomolecular Sequence Models
summary: Pretrained sequence models are now paired with explicit binding, off-target, and activity objectives across RNA, DNA, antibody, and TCR tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pretrained biomolecular sequence or representation models steered by an explicit constraint. GABIF runs guided discrete diffusion for antibody inverse folding, with an antibody-antigen binding affinity regressor steering sequence generation. Pep2Tcr conditions peptide-specific CDR3β generation through an encoder-decoder with contrastive learning. MARRI places opening penalties and hybridization gains inside cross-RNA attention over RNA foundation model representations, and PriMPT encodes prior information into multiscale paired-token representations of guide RNA-DNA pairs for Cas9 off-target cleavage. SIREN and DeepMolVir use language model embeddings alone, ranking small molecules for RNA targets from sequence and encoding viruses via ESMC-600M, respectively. What is new is the form of the constraint: a learned oracle, an explicit mechanistic term, or a conditioning input built into the model. Not every item applies constraints in this sense, so the shared direction is constrained use of pretrained sequence models rather than a uniform method.
